objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with chronic flank pain and a history of urinary tract infections.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve been having intermittent flank pain for about five months, and I’ve had five urinary tract infections over the past two years. I’m not having any recent fever, nausea, or vomiting, and my urinary frequency or urgency is only affected during the UTIs.
Have you noticed any blood in your urine—either visible red or pink discoloration, or detected on urine testing—during these episodes of flank pain or between your UTIs?
“Yes, I’ve noticed occasional blood-tinged urine during some of the UTI episodes, but I don’t usually have visible discoloration between infections.”
Is the flank pain sharp and colicky (coming in waves), or more of a constant dull ache, and does it radiate toward your groin or lower abdomen?
“It feels more like a constant dull ache most of the time, but sometimes it spikes with waves of pain. It can radiate toward my lower abdomen, but not so much into my groin.”
Have you ever been told you have kidney stones, or have you had any imaging studies (such as CT, ultrasound, or X-ray) of your kidneys that showed stones, obstruction, or structural abnormalities?
“No, I’ve never been told I have kidney stones, and I haven’t had any imaging studies of my kidneys—no CT or ultrasound to my knowledge.”
What is your age and sex?
I’m 31 years old and female.
Do your UTIs tend to occur in relation to sexual activity—for example, shortly after intercourse?
“Sometimes the UTIs seem to flare after sexual activity, though I can’t say it’s perfectly every time. I haven’t noticed any specific timing pattern other than that general association.”
Have you ever had urinary tract infections or kidney problems as a child, or been evaluated with voiding cystourethrograms or other tests for vesicoureteral reflux?
I haven’t had kidney or urinary problems as a child, and I’ve never been evaluated with tests like a voiding cystourethrogram for reflux. No one has mentioned vesicoureteral reflux to me before.
Does the flank pain occur specifically during your UTI episodes, or do you also experience it when you don't have an active infection?

“I’d say the flank pain is worse during the UTI episodes, but I do still notice it intermittently even when I don’t feel like I’m actively infected. It doesn’t seem to fully go away between infections.”
Do you ever experience difficulty starting your urine stream, a weak stream, or a sensation that your bladder doesn't fully empty after urinating?

Patient: I don’t usually have difficulty starting my stream or a weak stream, and I generally feel like I empty my bladder completely. Occasionally I notice some discomfort with urination during the UTIs, but that’s mainly when I’m having the infection symptoms.
Do you have any family history of kidney stones, kidney disease, or early-onset hypertension?

I don’t have any known family history of kidney stones, kidney disease, or early-onset hypertension. However, I can’t say with certainty about every relative’s history, but nothing has been brought to my attention.
Is the flank pain consistently on one side (right or left), or does it occur on both sides?
“It’s mostly on one side—I’d say primarily the left flank—but occasionally I feel it on the other side too, though less often.”
Does your flank pain or the blood in your urine ever coincide with your menstrual period?
Patient: “I haven’t noticed a clear pattern with my menstrual period—no consistent timing where the flank pain or the blood-tinged urine shows up right around my period.”
Have all of your UTIs been confirmed with urine cultures, and if so, were they caused by the same type of bacteria each time (such as E. coli), or different organisms?

“I’m not 100% sure, but I believe they were confirmed with urine cultures during most of the episodes. I don’t know whether the bacteria were the same each time—my records only sometimes mentioned the organism, and I haven’t kept track of patterns.”
Have you ever noticed any small stones, gravel, or sand-like material passing in your urine, or felt a sudden relief of pain after passing something in your urine?
“I haven’t noticed any small stones or gravel in my urine, and I don’t recall a sudden relief after passing anything. The pain tends to ease gradually, especially as the UTI symptoms improve.”

[DDX] Nephrolithiasis (kidney stone, possibly struvite/staghorn), Ureteropelvic junction obstruction, Chronic pyelonephritis/renal abscess, Complicated renal cyst (hemorrhagic or infected), Ureteral stricture
